theory: A flask with a narrow neck is a Helmholtz resonator: the plug of air in the neck oscillates on the spring of the air in the bulb. Its resonant frequency is
where $c$ is the speed of sound, $A$ the neck's cross-sectional area, $V$ the air volume and $L'$ the neck length plus its end corrections.

Adding a volume $V_w$ of water leaves air volume $V = V_0 - V_w$, so $\dfrac{1}{f^{2}} = \dfrac{4\pi^{2}L'}{c^{2}A}\,(V_0 - V_w)$: a straight line against $V_w$ with a negative slope that meets the $V_w$-axis at $V_0$.
That line is the calibration: measure the resonant frequency for an unknown amount of water and read its volume from the line.

apparatus.flask: Flask resonator: a round flask with a narrow neck.
apparatus.cylinder: Measuring cylinder: 100 ml with 1 ml graduations.
apparatus.generator: Signal generator with a frequency display.
apparatus.speaker: Small loudspeaker held at the mouth of the flask.
apparatus.thermometer: Thermometer for the air temperature (for the speed of sound).

safety: Keep water away from the signal generator and its leads.
Keep the loudspeaker volume low; long exposure to loud tones is harmful.
steps: Switch on the loudspeaker at the mouth of the empty flask.
Sweep the frequency slowly to find where the sound is loudest. Record V_w = 0 and f.
Fill the measuring cylinder, read it at the bottom of the meniscus, and pour the water into the flask.
Find the new resonant frequency. Record the total volume of water added and f.
Repeat until the flask is about two-thirds full (at least six readings).
Empty the flask, pour in the unknown sample and record its resonant frequency as f (unknown).
Work out 1/f², plot 1/f² against V_w, and use the line to find V₀ and the unknown volume.
tips: Keep a running total of the water you have poured in.
Sweep up and down through the resonance: the loudest point is easier to find from both sides.
1/f² is small: write it in standard form, e.g. 2.84 × 10⁻⁵ s².
references: Kinsler, L. E. et al. Fundamentals of Acoustics, ch. 10 (the Helmholtz resonator).

frequencyFalls.title: The frequency falls as water is added
frequencyFalls.detail: More water leaves less air in the bulb, so the resonant frequency should rise. Re-check these readings and your running total of water.

noUnknown.title: Use your calibration
noUnknown.detail: Measure the resonant frequency of the unknown sample and record it as f (unknown); your result will read its volume off your line.
